title: Applied ML Eval Harness, Prompt Sets, Quantization Profiles, and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Evelyn Park
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood's applied-ML evaluation practices: the eval harness, canonical prompt-set and benchmark guidance, model onboarding checklists, quality guardrails, quantization profile expectations, and the regression triage process. The audience is ML engineers, applied researchers, and platform owners responsible for model serving quality and release readiness. This document standardizes how we run automated and manual evals, how we respond to regressions, and how quantization and rollout decisions are documented.

Goals
- Reduce production regressions by ensuring consistent pre-release eval coverage.
- Provide clear, actionable triage steps and ownership during regressions.
- Standardize prompt/benchmark hygiene to make evals comparable across models and versions.
- Ensure quantization profiles have measurable quality impact bounds.

Scope
Includes: eval harness configuration, prompt set curation, onboarding checklist for new model variants, quality guardrails (metrics and thresholds), quantization profile requirements, and the regression triage playbook. Excludes: research experiments that are not intended for serving, and ad-hoc debug scripts.

Ownership and Contacts
- Primary owner: Applied ML Platform (applied-ml@redwood.com)
- Responsible engineers: Evelyn Park (author), Aisha Malik (eval-harness), Marco Gonzalez (quantization)
- Oncall / Escalation: eng-sre oncall (see eng-sre/runbooks)

Glossary and Key Concepts
- Eval harness: the CI-integrated system and workflow that runs model-level metrics across prompt sets and testbeds.
- Prompt set: curated inputs representing production use-cases; categorized by vertical, complexity, and known failure modes.
- Quality guardrails: metric thresholds (e.g., ROUGE, accuracy, hallucination score, safety flags) that determine pass/fail for a rollout.
- Quantization profile: a named combination of bit-widths, per-layer strategies, and calibration parameters used to produce a serving artifact.
- Regression triage: the incident-like process for investigating and remediating declines in core metrics or customer-reported quality issues.

1) Eval Harness: Standards and Configuration
Intro: The eval harness executes deterministic runs for each candidate model and produces a standardized report (JSON + HTML summary) that is uploaded to the model onboarding ticket and to the eval dashboard.

Minimum harness outputs (required on every run):
- summary.json (model, commit, dataset versions, pass/fail flags)
- metrics.csv (per-prompt metrics and aggregations)
- example_fails/ (top-N failure examples with inputs, reference, and model output)

Recommended CI integration:
1. Run unit-level smoke tests on PRs.
2. On merge to main: schedule a full eval job against the canonical prompt sets and quantization profiles.
3. On candidate model release (staging): run a continuous A/B evaluation comparing candidate vs baseline for 48-72 hours against sampled production traffic (if traffic capture enabled).

Sample eval-harness CLI (example):
python -m eval_harness.run --model artifact://models/my-model:2026-07-01 --prompt-set canonical-v2 --quant-profile int8-v3 --output ./artifacts/run-2026-07-01

2) Prompt Sets and Benchmark Hygiene
Principles for prompt sets:
- Coverage: include representative prompts for high-volume routes, critical edge cases, and known failure classes.
- Label-led: prompts should include metadata: intent, complexity, sensitivity, and expected output format.
- Versioned: every change to a prompt set increments a semantic version and includes a migration note.
- Size: canonical prompt sets should be sized for statistical confidence (minimum 1,000 examples where applicable) or smaller curated sets (100-500) for targeted regression checks.

Required fields for a prompt-set manifest (CSV/JSON):
- id, text, intent_tag, expected_label/format, difficulty, sensitivity_flag, created_by, created_at, source_reference

Example manifest row (CSV):
12345,"Summarize the following email...","summarization","summary_text","medium","no","data-team","2026-04-10","jira-456"

Benchmarks and evaluation metrics
- For NLU tasks: accuracy, F1, confusion breakdown.
- For generation: BLEU/ROUGE where applicable, semantic similarity (embedding-based), and a human-eval sample for subjective quality.
- Safety and hallucination: safety flag rate, hallucination score (custom metric), and counterfactual checks.
- Latency and cost: 95th pct latency on target hardware profile, per-token cost estimate.

3) Model Onboarding Checklist
Before a model is approved for serving the following must be completed: 
- Documentation: model card, intended capabilities, failure modes, and privacy considerations.
- Eval harness: full canonical-v2 run passed or documented exceptions.
- Regression comparison: candidate vs baseline runs with delta table showing per-route impact. 
- Quantization checks: if a quantized artifact will be used in production, attach quantization report (see section 5).
- Canary plan: runtime config for a canary, sample size, rollback criteria, and monitoring links.
- Security review: if model training used customer data, ensure data usage review completed.

Approval flow (high level):
1. Author creates onboarding ticket and attaches eval artifacts.
2. Applied ML owner reviews and requests changes if needed.
3. Product and SRE sign off on canary plan.
4. Model is scheduled for canary and follow-up A/B evaluation.

4) Quality Guardrails and Thresholds
Guardrail categories and default thresholds (modify per use-case):
- Functional correctness: task-specific metric delta <= 0.5% relative to baseline for high-volume routes; <=2% for experimental routes.
- Safety: safety-flag rate must not increase by more than 0.1 percentage points absolute or exceed an absolute 0.5% rate for non-sensitive routes. For sensitive routes the absolute cap is 0.05%.
- Hallucination: average hallucination score increase <= 0.5 points (on the configured 0-5 scale).
- Latency: p95 latency increase <= 10% vs baseline on target hardware.
- Cost: per-token cost increase <= 15% unless compensated by a customer-approved price change.

Guardrail enforcement policy:
- Fail-fast: a single required guardrail failure blocks automated promotion to production.
- Documented exceptions: owners must create an exception ticket with a mitigation plan and explicit timelines.

5) Quantization Profiles and Quality Expectations
Profile naming: <strategy>-<bits>-<calibration>-v<major> (e.g., perchannel-int8-adaptive-v2)
Required artifacts: quant_report.json, per-layer error table (CSV), example_fails_quantized/ sample outputs.
Quantization validation steps:
1. Produce quantized model artifact with reproducible script.
2. Run canonical prompt-set comparison: compare baseline FP16 vs quantized using the eval harness.
3. Check per-task metric deltas against guardrails.
4. Run targeted downstream integration smoke tests (e.g., structured-output parsers).

Quantization acceptance criteria (default):
- Aggregate metric delta <= 1.0% relative for core tasks; per-route exceptions require approvals.
- No regression in safety flags beyond thresholds in section 4.
- Top-10 human-evaluated failure examples do not show systematic output corruption.

6) Regression Triage Playbook (incident-style flow)
Trigger conditions (examples):
- Canary A/B test shows significant drop per guardrails.
- Production monitoring alerts: sudden spike in error rate, customer-reported quality issues, or new safety-flag increase.

Immediate steps (0-30 minutes):
1. Acknowledge: assign an incident owner and create a regression triage ticket in JIRA with prefix REG-YYYY.
2. Collect context: model version, route(s) impacted, recent deployments, eval-harness summary, and a sample of failing requests.
3. Short-term mitigation: if severity is high, route traffic to baseline model variant or increase fallback thresholds.

Investigation steps (30-240 minutes):
1. Reproduce locally: run eval harness against the reported prompt subset and full canonical sets.
2. Compare model artifacts: check commit differences, tokenizer changes, and quantization profile differences.
3. Check infra signals: GPU queueing, batching anomalies, and KV-cache corruption possibilities.
4. Run targeted human evaluation on top failure examples.

Remediation and follow-through (4 hours - 14 days):
- Hotfix: deploy rollback to baseline or deploy a quick fix quant/profile revert.
- Root cause analysis: document root cause, remediation actions, and follow-up items.
- Postmortem: for regressions that triggered production impact or customer complaints, produce a postmortem within 7 days and link to the triage ticket.
- Preventative actions: add new prompts to canonical sets, adjust guardrails, or update quant profiles as needed.

Decision matrix for rollback vs fix:
- Severity high (customer impact or safety break): immediate rollback to baseline.
- Severity medium: consider partial traffic reduction with aggressive monitoring.
- Severity low: schedule a patch and monitor A/B results.

7) Reporting and Continuous Improvement
- Every triage ticket must include a short summary with metrics, affected routes, and remediation status.
- Weekly digest: applied-ml publishes a weekly digest (Slack + confluence) summarizing new regressions, root causes, and lessons learned.
- Quarterly review: update canonical prompt sets and quantization profile baselines based on drift observed in production.

Appendices
A. Example eval-harness JSON summary (trimmed)
{
  "model": "models/my-model:2026-07-01",
  "prompt_set": "canonical-v2",
  "metrics": { "summarization_rouge_l": 0.78, "safety_flag_rate": 0.002 },
  "pass": false
}

B. Quick links
- Eval harness repo: git@github.com:redwood-inference/eval-harness
- Prompt set catalog: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks
- Quantization profiles: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles

C. Example labels and manifest fields for prompt sets (CSV header)
id,text,intent_tag,expected_label,difficulty,sensitivity_flag,created_by,created_at,source_reference

D. Frequently asked questions
Q: How do we decide which prompts become part of canonical-v2?
A: Prompts are selected by coverage (traffic-weighted), known failure classes, and product-critical scenarios. Changes require review by the Applied ML owners and are communicated in the weekly digest.

Q: When is an exception allowed for a quantized profile?
A: Exceptions require documented trade-offs, a mitigation timeline, and approval from Applied ML and Product.
